small_guidance:
- The fused ReLU+GroupNorm is already cheap; the dominant cost is `nn.ConvTranspose3d`. Minor tuning (BLOCK_S=2048, num_warps=8, num_stages=2, vectorized 4-wide loads) on the norm kernel will not close the gap to baseline=7.0ms.
- If staying with tuning, switch the norm kernel to channels-last layout for the group axis and use one program per (N, G) with a single-pass Welford to avoid two reads of x.
- Fold ReLU into the conv epilogue once the conv is custom — keep the GN kernel as the only post-conv pass.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: program tiles over (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile); for each input voxel compute the outer product with the 3x3x3 kernel slice and `tl.atomic_add` into the output grid at the correct (od,oh,ow) positions (stride=1, pad=0, so out_dim = in_dim + 2). This eliminates the heavy cuDNN deconv call which dominates the 10ms runtime.
- Alternatively, since stride=1 and kernel=3, implement ConvTranspose3d as a *gather* direct-conv with implicit zero-padding of 2 on the input and a flipped kernel — one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), accumulating over IC*27. This avoids atomics and maps cleanly to a GEMM-style tile (BLOCK_OC=32/64, BLOCK_S=64/128, BLOCK_K=IC).
- Fuse ReLU into the conv epilogue (apply `tl.maximum(acc,0)` before store) and write to a channels-last layout so the subsequent GroupNorm kernel reads contiguously along the reduction axis. Keep GN as one program per (N, G) with single-pass Welford.
